heading: Absolute coordinates
text:
### Absolute coordinates [LTSL.3.2]

A test may instead use absolute coordinates — a `calendar.time` call in the `at`
/ `until` position, e.g. `at calendar.time(2026, 6, 18, 14, 0, 0):` — when the
calendar date is load-bearing ([LTIM.14.1]). A test must use one mode
throughout, recorded on the compiled test case (`TestCase.absolute_time`).
An author testing a rule that reads the calendar from `now()` should use absolute
coordinates, since in relative mode the rule reads a date in 1970 ([LTSL.3.1]). An
absolute coordinate sets the wall clock to its instant and advances the monotonic
clock ([LTIM.2.8.2]) by the interval since the previous coordinate.
